deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.11): k is a commutative ring and P is a small k-linear category. P^& = Hom_k(P^o, Ab_k) is the category of additive presheaves of k-modules. For a k-additive category M (with enough colimits), P^&_M = Hom_k(P^o, M) is the category of M-valued presheaves. For L in P^& and x in M there is an external tensor L ⊗_k x in P^&_M. For F in P^&_M and L' in P^{o&} there is the coend tensor product F ⊛_k L' = ∫^a F(a) ⊗_k L'(a), an object of M. Page 11 proved two things. First, (L⊗x) ⊛ L' ≅ (L ⊛ L') ⊗ x; in particular (h_a ⊗ x) ⊛ L' ≅ L'(a) ⊗_k x. Second, L ⊗ x is projective when L and x are projective. It then asked whether P^&_M has enough projectives, so that Tor_i(F, L') can be defined.

This page answers that question and sets up the derived (balanced) tensor product F ⊛^L_k L'.

Left column, first part. One defines F· ⊛^L L· by taking a projective resolution of F· and applying ⊛ termwise. One wants a quasi-isomorphism L· → L'· to induce a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring. This requires the projective objects of P^&_N to be 'flat' for the tensor product. There is also a garbled general remark about a 'big' Q^& of a category whose objects should be flat.

Left column, second part. He axiomatizes what he calls, in an inserted note, a 'k-flat' category N:
- N is k-additive and Karoubian.
- (a) N has small sums.
- (b) A small sum of monomorphisms is a monomorphism (an AB4-type condition).
- (c) Every object is a quotient of a projective.
- (d) For every projective x, the functor Ab_k → N, U ↦ U ⊗_k x, preserves monomorphisms.

Right column (final version). Let N be k-additive, Karoubian, with small sums.

(a) Suppose N has enough projectives. Then every F in P^&_N is a quotient of ℒ = ⊕_{a ∈ Ob P} h_a ⊗_k x_a, where each x_a is projective and x_a → F(a) is an epimorphism. Such an ℒ is projective, using the corollary on p.11 and the fact that sums of projectives are projective.

(b) Suppose further that U ↦ U ⊗_k x is exact for each projective x. Since this functor is left adjoint to Hom(x, −), it is automatically right exact, so exactness means preserving monomorphisms. Then for every projective ℒ the functor P^{o&} → N, L' ↦ ℒ ⊛ L', is exact. Indeed, it equals L' ↦ ⊕_a L'(a) ⊗ x_a (or a direct summand of this), by the formula on p.11. Each summand is exact, and the sum is exact by the AB4-type hypothesis.

Consequently F· ⊛^L L'· can be computed by projective resolutions ℒ· of F· alone, and it sends quasi-isomorphisms in the L' variable to quasi-isomorphisms. This is the standard construction of a Tor/derived tensor product of a functor with coefficients in N against a k-module-valued functor. It is what one needs for homology of (k-linear) categories with coefficients, which is presumably the 'abelianization' purpose of the dossier.

The computer listing on which the notes are written is dated 16 Sep 82, with the line 'Arrêt de l'ordinateur: vendredi 17 septembre'. This gives a terminus post quem of mid-September 1982 for the page.
errors: In the left-column condition d) and in b) of the right column he writes U ↦ U ⊗_k a with a projective in N. Elsewhere a denotes objects of P, so this should read x (the right column does say 'objet projectif x'). This is a notational slip.

The claim that a quasi-isomorphism L· → L'· induces a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring with a projective resolution of F· is only automatic for bounded-above complexes. For unbounded complexes one needs K-projective resolutions, or AB4/AB4* control of the totalization. The page does not state a boundedness hypothesis.

Defining U ⊗_k x for an arbitrary k-module U requires cokernels in N (presentation U = coker(k^(J) → k^(I))), not just Karoubian with sums. The previous page assumed 'stable par lim', which covers this, but the final right-column hypotheses omit it.

ideas.what: Existence of enough projectives in the functor category Hom_k(P^o, N): generators h_a ⊗ x with x projective in N.
ideas.modern_name: Projective generators of functor categories / representable-tensor-projective generators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Mitchell 'Rings with several objects' 1972; Freyd; Oberst–Röhrl)
ideas.where_published: Analogous generator arguments appear in Tohoku (1957) for functor categories; not this exact form.

ideas.what: Flatness of projective functors for the coend tensor product, reduced to exactness of U ↦ U ⊗_k x on projectives plus AB4 in N; definition of a 'k-flat' category.
ideas.modern_name: Tensored (copowered) k-linear category with flat projectives; balanced derived tensor product of bimodule-type functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard homological algebra (Cartan–Eilenberg balance of Tor; Mitchell; Quillen-style homology of categories; Baues–Wirsching for coefficients)

ideas.what: Derived tensor product F ⊛^L_k L' of an N-valued functor with a k-module-valued functor, computed by projective resolution of one variable only.
ideas.modern_name: Derived coend / Tor of functors over a k-linear category with coefficients in an abelian category (derived functor tensor product)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mitchell 1972; Keller (derived categories of dg categories, 1994) for the dg version

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine homological algebra for functor categories: enough projectives, flatness of projectives, and a balanced derived tensor product. All of this is well established in the literature. Its main interest is historical. The computer printout dates the page to after 16–17 September 1982, and it documents Grothendieck working out 'abelianization' and homology with coefficients shortly before Pursuing Stacks.
transcription_corrections: 'p𝓛^&_N' is almost certainly 'P^&_N' (the functor category Hom_k(P^o, N)).
In the right column b), the functor 'Q^& → N, L' ↦ ℒ ⊗_k L'' has source P^{o&} (L' ranges over P^{o&} as on p.11); the handwritten letter is possibly a script P with superscript o&.
In the right column b), 'pour [-?-] objet projectif x' reads 'pour tout objet projectif x de N'.
In the final lines, 'résolutions projectives F· de F·' should be read as projective resolutions ℒ· of F·.
The computer listing under the notes reads 'DERNIERE MISE A JOUR DE JOURNAL : 13-09-8[2]' / 'ARRET DE L'ORDINATEUR : VENDREDI 17 SEPTEMBRE DE 7 H A 8 H', with job lines dated 16 SEP 82.
